messages:
Andy K: Heads up 3 MaritimeDX wants a private deployment POC. Key network asks: preserve original client IPs for audit, single static egress IP for their firewall, and allow an on-prem TLS inspection box in the path. Any red flags?
Priya S: Quick summary: PrivateLink easiest to stand up, but it presents traffic from our ENIs -> customer sees our IPs. If they need true client src IP on their on-prem proxy, PrivateLink alone won't give it.
Liao C: We can add X-Forwarded-For or a custom header, but that requires trust and config on their proxy to use that header for audit logs. Not ideal if they mandate network-level source IPs.
Nora M: For full preservation you need a route-preserving topology: VPC peering or TGW+VPN/Direct where packets keep original client source IP. That implies more changes on their side (route tables, permissions) and longer lead time.
Andy K: They asked about implications for TLS inspection. They plan to terminate TLS in their on-prem proxy (MITM). Will that change anything for us?
Liao C: If they terminate TLS on-prem, we can do TCP passthrough to their proxy. PrivateLink -> ENI -> proxy chain still means their proxy sees our ENI src IPs. If they want client IPs and are doing TLS inspection, they'd need our stack to forward headers or for clients to connect directly into their ingress (not common).
Priya S: Also call out SNI and cert pinning caveat: if they inspect and rewrite certs, apps with pinning will break. Document this for security team.
Nora M: Firewall allowlist snippet we can give them now: ```Customer proxies (ingress rules): Allow from 10.10.0.0/22 -> proxy: 443 (TCP)``` ```Egress allowlist (to accept our POC egress): 3.101.45.99/32 (POC EIP, region us-west-2)``` Add note: replace with final EIP(s) after provisioning.
Andy K: Good. What about NAT behavior? If we host in their account (Private deployment), can we avoid NAT so they see client IPs?
Liao C: If our pods/instances live in their VPC and we don't hairpin/NAT, then yes—but our Private deployment architecture uses managed ENIs and often a NAT for control plane egress. We can request a config where customer provides NAT gateway or routes to preserve source IPs, but it's a custom setup and needs network ops signoff.
Priya S: TL;DR options to present to customer: 1) PrivateLink + XFF header (fast, low friction). 2) VPC peering / TGW + VPN/Direct (preserves src IP, slower setup). 3) Host all nodes in their VPC with custom routing (works but requires runbook + infra changes).
Nora M: Add pricing note for the sales thread: POC usually billed as short-term private license + small reserved capacity; we may charge for static EIP allocation and extra network engineering hours if they want custom routing.
Andy K: They also asked for short answers for their security questionnaire about network logging and keys. Can we provide bullet points?
Priya S: Sure: - Network logging: VPC Flow Logs + application audit logs can be streamed to the customer's logging sink. - TLS: TLS1.2+/TLS1.3 enforced; control-plane mTLS available. - KMS: BYOK supported for data-at-rest via customer-managed KMS in Private deployments. - Change control: We'll run infra changes via their ticketing + scheduled maintenance windows.
Liao C: Ops caveats to call out: - If they insist on source IP preservation for end-user metrics, we'll need to validate middleware assumptions (XFF vs netlogs). - Peering may introduce asymmetric routing if they have multiple TGW attachments 3 test thoroughly. - NACLs are stateless; ensure both inbound/outbound allowed for ephemeral ports.
infra-bot: POC ticket created: POC-8022, assigned to eng-platform. Network presubmit ETA: 72 hours. :white_check_mark:
Andy K: I'll send this back to MaritimeDX network team and ask if X-Forwarded-For is acceptable or if they require native src IPs. Thanks all. :pray:
